title: The clitellum’s deception: phylogenetic and morphological insights into the Allolobophora molleri–moebii (Crassiclitellata: Lumbricidae) earthworm species complex
content:
Abstract
Adaptation to soil environments has simplified body plans in earthworms, often yielding morphologically uniform species despite substantial genetic diversity. Conversely, some taxa show marked external variation with limited genetic differentiation. The Allolobophora molleri–moebii complex exemplifies this pattern, as several morphologically distinct species have been described mainly by clitellum position. To assess its taxonomy, specimens from 43 localities in Portugal, Spain, and Morocco were analysed using integrated morphological and molecular approaches. Multilocus phylogenetic analyses based on six loci revealed strong geographic structure with no correspondence to the currently recognized species: individuals assigned to different species frequently clustered together. Clitellum position varied continuously across individuals, and multivariate analyses showed broad overlap among traditional species, preventing clear diagnostic boundaries. Haplotypes were widely shared across nominal taxa, and species-delimitation methods produced inconsistent partitions that did not support current species boundaries. Time-calibrated analyses placed the split from the sister group in the Oligocene and a major diversification during the Miocene, supporting an Iberian origin followed by secondary dispersal across the present distribution. Integrated molecular and morphological evidence supports synonymizing the entire complex under Allolobophora molleri, with A. moebii, A. fernandae, A. opisthosellata, A. monchicana and Heraclescolex kionionus proposed as new junior synonyms (syn. nov.), highlighting this taxon as a model for exploring links between genomic variation, phenotypic diversity, and climatic adaptation in soil fauna.
